title: Caching Strategies: Cache-Aside vs Write-Through
subtitle: How large-scale distributed systems achieve sub-millisecond reads
summary: Caching places high-frequency data in lightning-fast in-memory stores (like Redis or Memcached) to prevent exhausting your primary database.
key_points: Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading): The application first checks cache. If cache miss, reads from DB and writes to cache. Great for read-heavy workloads.
Write-Through: App writes data to the cache, which immediately writes to the DB. High consistency, slightly slower write latency.
Eviction Policies: LRU (Least Recently Used) is most common. LFU (Least Frequently Used) is best for long-term popularity curves.
interview_tip: In interviews, always bring up Cache Invalidation ('There are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things').
